#3297. The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

The “Siri Recap” feature that Apple announced in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that launched at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

The recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":

Music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

Sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this launched in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

Live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just said in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

But Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an update on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

At least for now, the feature is only available in a developer beta, so sign up for that now if you want to try it. You'll need an Apple Watch Series 12 (or Ultra 4) and an iPhone 16 or better, excluding the 16e. (I have a 16 Pro, so I'm good.)

After you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

But still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people said to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.)

Because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

When it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

Details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

But it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most important points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

And there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

#3295. 10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

If you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

Reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

Old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access

Many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

A multireddit is a feed that shows posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in new Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

After all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

#3294. Could ‘Rubber Soul’ Be the Best Beatles Album? (Yes)

Fall is always Rubber Soul Season. The Beatles’ 1965 masterpiece has always been autumn-coded, with its bristling guitars, wistful vocals, pensive lyrics. But this fall, Rubber Soul has been in the air even more than usual, because of the phenomenal new Special Edition, which gets you up close with John, Paul, George, and Ringo like never before. Their most emotional album. Their moodiest. Their wittiest. Their best.

So what is it that makes Rubber Soul the Beatles’ best album? It’s a loaded question, but for some of us, there’s a correct answer, and it’s simple: It all comes down to the singing. In addition to everything else it is, Rubber Soul is the best place to hear John, Paul, George, and Ringo sing together. It’s four boys telling their stories out loud—you can hear them puzzling out the tales as they sing, bouncing ideas off each other, daring each other to dig a little deeper.

Over the decades, each era chooses its own Beatles album to deify as the ultimate Fabs masterpiece. In the vinyl era, it was Sgt. Pepper; the CD era chose Revolver; the streaming era has anointed Abbey Road. It would be diplomatic and civilized to say that all these albums are equally great…but this will never do, because we all take our own personal Beatles so seriously, and you’d have to be some kind of Mr. Mustard to pretend you don’t have a favorite, and for me, that’s always been Rubber Soul.

The Beatles had to bash out this album in a hurry, in October 1965, to rush some product into the shops in time for Christmas. They wrote seven of the songs in a week, pushing the deadline right down to the final hours. But they had a phenomenal hot streak. (Or should we say, it once had them?) Even the quickies have soul — like “Michelle,” a trifle Paul wrote in his teens for the specific purpose of wooing Liverpool art-student girls by pretending to be French.

But the thing that makes Rubber Soul stand out, head and moptops above the rest, is the singing, with these four boys mingling their voices, each sha-la-la and each na-na-na, each in-my-life and no-I-wouldn’t so charged with raw emotion. Their voices were changing from boys to men — Ringo and John were 25, Paul 23, George 22 — and you can hear their irresistible excitement that they can now emote as the world-weary men they always aspired to be. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Just a year earlier, in tunes like “I’m a Loser” and “No Reply,” John was trying to sing like a gritty Dylan-esque folk rogue; now he not only had the voice to pull it off, he could write tunes to match. Paul had never sounded so rugged as he did in “I’m Looking Through You,” but never so boyish as he does in the middle eight of “Wait.” The way he purrs “I feel as though you ought to know,” he sounds so guileless, even though he’s cheerfully admitting he’s been cheating like crazy on the road. (That “I’ve been good, as good as I can be” is an all-time Paul line reading.)

George, after playing grown-up with his voice on Help! (with the magnificently boyish “I Need You” and “You Like Me Too Much”), got all the way there. Why was the Quiet One suddenly using words like “opaque” and “rectify”? Because his groovy mod wife Pattie Boyd bought him a thesaurus, hoping it would help him write some eloquent love songs to tell the world about her. It’s safe to say “Think for Yourself” wasn’t what she had in mind.

But that’s just the lead vocals, which are only part of the story here, because you can get lost forever immersing yourself in the background vocals. None of them are holding back, no matter whose song it is. Listen to what Paul adds to “Norwegian Wood” or “Nowhere Man” or “If I Needed Someone”; listen to what John brings to “You Won’t See Me” or “Wait.” In the vivid new remix from Giles Martin and Sam Okell, you can go deeper than ever into these harmonies. Related Content Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr to Reunite at Las Vegas Show in 2027 What's It Like to Write Songs With Madonna, McCartney, and the Stones? 50 Years Ago Today: Paul McCartney Wraps Up the Greatest Tour of His Post-Beatles Career Here Are the Best Podcasts About Songwriting

The lads were cranking around the clock to get Rubber Soul finished. They didn’t go into the studio with a plan to revolutionize pop music; they went in with a deadline. Nobody was asking for a great work of art— nobody except themselves, and their genius producer George Martin, who believed in them no matter what. The “harpsichord” solo in “In My Life”: That’s Mr. Martin, who went into the studio early, played his composed solo at half-speed on piano, sped it up to fit the tempo, then played it for the lads’ approval. That’s the spirit of collective make-it-work energy that made Rubber Soul come out as vibrant and fluent and unfettered as it is.

The pace was set right on the first day at Abbey Road, when John brought in two songs, from opposite sides of the genius spectrum: “Norwegian Wood,” a candidly introspective tale of getting outmaneuvered by a smarter operator, and “Run for Your Life,” a cheap Elvis joke that John somehow turned into one of his saddest, loneliest, most self-loathing vocals. “Run for Your Life” is the kind of song you’d bring to the studio if you scared yourself with how vulnerable you got in “Norwegian Wood.”

But both songs tell the truth about John’s miserable psyche in 1965. John was a recluse in his mansion, totally dependent on the Beatles as his only friends. He rarely even saw his wife or son without the TV blaring. He was a nowhere man, all right, and he told the truth about it in these songs. It might sound bizarre to think John brought in these different tunes the same day — yet it feels like “Run for Your Life” was a joke for him to hide behind, in case the other lads laughed at him for baring his soul in “Norwegian Wood.”

But they didn’t laugh. All four threw themselves into this song, wholeheartedly. George Harrison brought in an instrument he was still learning to play — he got it wrong, but came up with one of the most seductive sounds on any Beatles record, while Paul lifted John’s story with his ruggedly bruised vocals. (Rubber Soul is the place to start appreciating Paul’s underrated generosity as a team player; you don’t even notice him in “Norwegian Wood” or “If I Needed Someone,” until you do, but that’s when you realize how selflessly he’s elevating his fellow Beatles’ songs, and how bravely they wrote when they knew they could count on Paul covering their asses.)

There are no happy endings on the album — it’s the first Beatles album where none of the songs have “love” in the title, even though there’s a song about the word “love.” When Paul wrote his Rubber Soul songs, he was 23, the age Olivia Rodrigo is now — he really does seem pretty sad for a boy in love. (It’s the right age to be singing, “Love has a nasty habit of disappearing overnight.”)

But the dominant emotion here — in the voices and melodies far more than mere lyrics — is curiosity, as the boys chronicle a wide range of charismatic and complex women. Whether it’s John in “Girl” and “Norwegian Wood,” or George in “If I Needed Someone” and “Think for Yourself,” or Paul in “You Won’t See Me” and “I’m Looking Through You,” they’re on a quest to learn from these female characters, to communicate in their languages. (Even a goof like “Michelle” is about struggling to understand her native tongue; all we know about Michelle is she’s not learning Paul’s language at all.)

The first line of the album is John and Paul singing, “Asked a girl what she wanted to be.” In 1965, that was a question asked of boys, not girls. But the women on Rubber Soul have jobs, they have plans, they have interior lives and philosophical questions — none of them are waiting for a man, not even a Beatle.

On the final night of the sessions, they still needed two more songs to finish the album. So they showed up with two of their best: John’s “Girl” and Paul’s “You Won’t See Me.” You can hear the strain in their throats — you can also hear them revel in it. But all over Rubber Soul, you hear the Beatles listen to each other, openly imitating each other. They tell the truth about themselves by singing together.

As for “In My Life,” it’s the only Lennon-McCartney song where John and Paul seriously disputed who wrote it, which says a lot about how deep this song reached into both boys’ souls. John was eager to claim it for himself, while vacillating on how much Paul contributed. But in strictly musical terms, it has the Macca fingerprints all over, especially the “all these places had their moments” bridge.

As always, whichever Beatles are singing, you can hear their drummer listen to them and support them. No group of singers ever had a drummer like Ringo, and everybody always does their bravest singing when they’ve got Ringo behind them. He works hard to make himself easy to overlook — he always makes it a point of professional pride not to call attention to himself. “Singers love the way I play,” he told me in 2018. “I don’t play all over them.”

But he’s the heartbeat of these tunes — the singers go to all the personal places they visit because they know Ringo is lifting them up. In a song like “In My Life,” he makes it easy for John to be vulnerable, guiding him through these really difficult memories. That’s why every cover version falls flat — the song doesn’t soar without him. You can make a case for Abbey Road or Revolver as his drumming-is-my-madness peak, but Rubber Soul really shines as Ringo’s greatest hit.

The Special Edition adds both sides of the stand-alone single they cut at the sessions, “Day Tripper” and “We Can Work It Out.” There’s an instrumental take of “Day Tripper,” for those of us who love the guitars and percussion but not the vocal. To my personal (and undoubtedly wrong) perspective, it’s one of the lamest Beatles vocals, one of the few where they come off as phonies. Paul trying to sound disdainful and unimpressed by a girl is just out of his vocal skill set, the equivalent of Mick Jagger trying to sound sincere and sensitive. There’s an acoustic take where John and Paul sound far more charming, treating it as a joke — John can’t stop laughing at the final verse, which deserved no better.

The U.S. record company, as usual, tried to water down the album with an American version. However, they failed, because this version was arguably even better, kicking off with the double-whammy of “I’ve Just Seen a Face” and “Norwegian Wood” — is there a more euphoric five-minute intro to any album? “I’ve Just Seen a Face” came out that summer, on the original U.K. Help! There’s a great scene in the early Rolling Stones documentary Charlie Is My Darling where Mick and Keith are on tour in 1965, bored and dour in their hotel room, until Keith begins strumming “I’ve Just Seen a Face” and they sing it together — suddenly, even these bitchy Glimmer Twins can’t help grinning. Trending Stories Noel Fielding Says He Regrets 'Horrible' Jokes He Made With Russell Brand After Old Clip Resurfaces Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage Journey Go Their Separate Ways With Longtime Drummer The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For

Capitol didn’t plan on making Rubber Soul sound like a “folk-rock” album — when they pulled “I’ve Just Seen a Face” and “It’s Only Love” from Help!, they had no idea how Rubber Soul would sound. Neither did the Beatles, who hadn’t written the songs yet. But it’s the only case where the butchered U.S. version might top the original. The American Rubber Soul turned out to be even more influential — it’s the one that inspired Brian Wilson to make Pet Sounds, the one that challenged Bob Dylan to make Blonde on Blonde, the one that blew the minds of Marvin Gaye and Carole King and Stevie Wonder and the Grateful Dead.

I’ve spent my entire life trying and failing to make up my mind which one I love better, so it’s good to have both of them bundled together on the Special Edition. But either way, it settles the question of the Beatles’ greatest album. In my life, I love Rubber Soul more.

#3292. CMF Watch Pro review

The CMF Watch Pro is a basic smartwatch. It features 110 tracking modes, a secure fit, up to two weeks of battery life, and IP68 durability. However, there were data discrepancies and missing fitness-tracking stats, and I think the newer, cheaper CMF Watch 3 Pro is a better buy.

Can only be purchased through third-party sellers

Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

For anyone starting out on a fitness journey, one of the newest and best smartwatches isn’t always essential. You can still get useful metrics by using an older model, although I’m not sure the CMF Watch Pro is the answer for everyone.

There’s a lot to like about this watch, such as the durable build quality and the excellent battery life. It tracks 110 fitness modes and has a secure strap for HIIT workouts, but when it comes to data, there’s something missing.

There were discrepancies in the fitness data compared to other fitness trackers, and there was occasional missing data when tracking sleep and overall health. The watch face was also far too large for my wrist. To find out more, keep reading this full CMF Watch Pro review.

Accelerometer, heart rate monitor, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) sensor

The CMF Watch Pro is available to purchase from the third-party retailer AliExpress in the U.S. for $123 and in the U.K. for £109. The watch is available in four colors, including Dark Grey, Ash Grey, Silver and Orange.

The watch launched in September 2023 and has previously been available for as low as $69. However, it’s no longer available for purchase from Amazon or Nothing’s website, and its price has nearly doubled, so I wouldn’t recommend purchasing it anymore.

You can get the newer CMF Watch 3 Pro for the much lower price of $79, and it has more advanced features like dual-band GPS and 131 sport modes. It also has a circular watch face, which in my opinion looks sleeker, instead of the square face of the CMF Watch Pro.

If you just want to track wellness and don’t feel you need to look at a screen for your workout stats, the Fitbit Air is a great option for $99. This screen-free device can detect and track up to 100 sports and activities, and forgoes the distraction of a screen, which I personally love.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Amazfit Bip 6 is cheaper at $79 and performs far better. Sleep tracking is more accurate on the Bip 6 in comparison to the CMF Watch Pro. The Bip 6 can also track a wider variety of workouts.

CMF by Nothing is well known for its quirky design ethos, but the CMF Watch Pro seems to be a simple ode to the Apple Watch. With a square, 1.96-inch AMOLED touch-screen display, it feels very bulky on my wrist. It’s the same size as the larger variant of the Apple Watch Series 11. However, the CMF watch is nowhere near as chunky as the newer CMF Watch 3 Pro, which takes up more real estate on my arm.

The CMF Watch Pro has an aluminum alloy frame case, and it feels very sturdy. It took a few bumps while I was carrying out my daily tasks, but there are no scratches at all. The watch is very durable, with a rating of IP68, meaning it is completely dust-tight and can be submerged underwater. I wouldn’t recommend purchasing a watch with anything less than this level of protection, as you want it to be able to carry you through every activity. With that said, it’s not the best you can get. Other watches such as the Amazfit Bip 6 have a durability rating of 5ATM which means it can withstand underwater pressure, making it far better for sports.

There is a button on the right side, which cycles through watch settings, but it’s also touchscreen. The adjustable silicone wrist strap feels secure throughout workouts and didn’t cause any irritation.

The CMF Watch Pro can track up to 110 different sports. It has basic workouts like running, walking, weight training, and Pilates.

It counts my daily steps, tracks my heart rate throughout activities, and has smart detection to automatically recognise some activities. You can also sync the data it collects with third-party apps like Strava and Apple Health, but you can’t integrate these apps into the watch.

My average heart rate after each workout I measured was around the same as my Oura Ring 5, so I’d say the watch’s tracking here is pretty accurate. However, I noticed that my peak heart rate wasn’t the same — the CMF Watch Pro logged it a lot lower— and I logged around 700 steps less than my Oura Ring and phone each day. It’s a good-enough watch if you only need the very basics, but why not just purchase something similarly-priced with a bit more accuracy? I’d recommend the Amazfit Bip 6 or the Xiaomi Smart Band 10 for monitoring during workouts with more accuracy.

Health monitoring and sleep tracking are very basic on the CMF Watch Pro, and there are some discrepancies when compared to other devices, so this probably isn’t the best option for fitness fanatics.

The CMF Watch Pro’s health tracking capabilities are basic. There’s 24-hour heart rate tracking and blood oxygen monitoring, but no ECG. If you want this you’ll have to spend more on the Apple Watch Series 11. It can also track your stress. These are important metrics if you’re managing a health condition, however there was missing data and discrepancies during activity when compared to other tracking devices. The step counts were inaccurate when compared to my Oura Ring and my peak heart rate wasn’t always captured. I also experienced this issue when using the CMF Watch 3 Pro.

You can also set up reminders on the watch for hydration and standing up. I personally like the stand-up reminder; I sometimes need a nudge to take a stretch break.

Interestingly, sleep tracking on the CMF Watch Pro is more accurate than the CMF Watch 3 Pro. The CMF Watch Pro tracked my full sleep; however, it was unbroken, whereas my Oura Ring picked up some accurate wake times.

I found the sleep analysis in the Nothing X app very basic. Since I like to track my sleep to evaluate readiness to account for my training load, having more information about movement and getting feedback on readings is often very helpful. If that’s something you want, the Xiaomi Smart Band 10 is a great option for $51.

The CMF Watch Pro gets up to 13 days of battery life per charge, but heavy use decreases this to around 11 days, which is still impressive. It took an hour to fully charge. It has the same battery life rating as the CMF Watch 3 Pro, and the more I consider the two devices, there’s not much separating them apart from their shape and an upgraded GPS system.

When the CMF Watch Pro is in power-saving mode, you can get up to 45 days of use. This obviously limits what you can do and won’t track your metrics continuously, and at that point you may as well just have an analog watch on your wrist.

The CMF Watch Pro is a solid option for anyone buying their first smartwatch. More advanced watches can seem overwhelming; this is a great entry-level option with 110 tracking modes and a secure and reliable fit. The battery can last almost two weeks, and the IP68 rating means it’s ready for anything, so you don’t need to take it off.

However, the large face of the CMF Watch Pro wasn’t the best fit for my wrist and led to some missing data and discrepancies in my fitness tracking compared to other watches. you may as well buy the newer CMF Watch 3 Pro, as there’s not that much difference between the two, and weirdly, the new watch is cheaper.

#3290. 10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

If you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with shows you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

If PIN protection is enabled, users must enter a four-digit PIN when switching between profiles on a single account. This is intended as a parental control feature, since it's available on non-Kids profiles and can keep children from accessing more mature content on an adult's profile. However, you can also enable this feature to keep other users from seeing your viewing history and preferences or influencing your algorithm by watching their content under your profile (accidentally or on purpose). To set up a PIN, log into your account on Hulu's website, select your profile, and go to Manage Profiles > Parental Controls. You'll have to choose a PIN and enter your password to confirm the changes.

Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain shows. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

If you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

If you have a long list of shows and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

If you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

If you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized users may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

Hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download shows and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

If you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your plan. You can update your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

#3289. Looze Cannon Was Rapping Before You Met ‘Big Michael’

The latest viral earworm on social media has an uncanny resemblance to the King of Pop. “Big Michael Michael,” first born as a freestyle on the musician and content creator Looze Cannon’s livestream, has taken the internet by storm. Delivered in a cotton-soft register not unlike Jackson’s, the track has gone on to top the iTunes Hip-Hop/Rap chart and inspire a lip-sync video from Lil Baby. Earlier this month, Looze Cannon brought his “Big Michael” character to G Herbo’s show at Chicago’s United Center, performing in front of a nearly sold-out crowd.

“G Herbo, I think he did a post where he was singing a song, and the next thing I know, my management was just telling me, ‘Hey, Herbo wants you to come out at the United Center in Chicago and perform,’” Cannon tells Rolling Stone. “I was like, ‘What?’ I thought everybody was playing, but it was real. We got in the Sprinter and we drove straight from Detroit to Chicago. And next thing I know, I was on stage, man, having the biggest moment of my life.”

The crowd size was the biggest Looze Cannon, who’s been rapping in Detroit since the 2010s, had ever performed in front of. “I’ve been around some big crowds because I’ve always been on stages and stuff like that, but that was the biggest thus far, was the G Herbo show,” he says. “That was the most I’ve ever performed in front of all at once.”

Cannon is among a new generation of artists who, in addition to releasing music, have developed a career livestreaming and making online video content. In his videos, he uses an AI face filter to perform as Jackson and various other characters on his livestreams. After first premiering the character early last month, he officially released the single “Big Michael Michael” on October 24.

“I had no clue that ‘Big Michael Michael’ would take off like that because it was just me playing around,” he says. “And so I just look back and I just say, wow, man, I can’t blame anybody but God, man, because I’ve been doing this for a long time and to see how this transition to what it is, it’s unexplainable.”  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

A Detroit native, Cannon’s been releasing music since at least 2016, when he put out Looze Minded. In 2020, he released Lil Glen, followed by Now or Never in 2023. Even so, he says detractors try to discredit his current moment as merely a viral gimmick. “I knew my wittiness and my funniness would help push the music because what I learned throughout the years is you got to get the people,” he says. “A lot of rappers, sometimes they focus on being too cool and trying to put off an image that they think will propel them into stardom or whatever, and people lose sight of being who they are.”

While he says he isn’t a Michael Jackson impersonator, he credits the singer with making him want to pursue music.

“I’m a big Michael Jackson fan. Michael was the reason why I even really wanted to do music,” he says. “I knew that there’s so many different versions of the impersonators out there and things like that, but I analyzed the game. What is it that no one is doing? And I just hit the live button, man, with that filter on and just blacked out. I just blacked out and it happened.”

He’d already been trying out other characters on livestream. “I have over 10 characters and I haven’t really unleashed all of them yet,” he says. “I was on an app called BIGO LIVE where I did multiple characters.”

Cannon’s other characters include a version of Dr. Seuss who tells stories in costume. He says he’s preparing to shoot a movie based on another of his characters. For TikTok, he went with Jackson. “I chose Mike on the TikTok side because I just knew the shock value of what it would do,” he says. Related Content Paris Jackson Calls Estate Executor’s $109 Million Fee Request ‘Offensive,’ Seeks Reduction Michael Jackson’s Legendary Super Bowl Halftime Show Is Getting Its Own Documentary Noel Gallagher’s ‘MTV Unplugged’ Acoustic Guitar Fetches $300,000 at Auction Jaafar Jackson Hopes 'Michael' Sequel Will Give 'More Insight' Into Allegations From Singer's 'Point of View'

“I thought back on just implementing my music into what I do, or pretty much taking the characters that I do and implementing what I really do into those characters,” he says. “And so that’s where the freestyling and doing the song, the parody songs, came into play.”

Cannon says commenters have mocked his advice to “be yourself” because he’s impersonating someone else. “They’re only looking at the surface of the filter,” he notes.

“None of them do what I do,” Cannon says of people who think his content doesn’t require skill or talent. “And it’s a reason for that because I’m actually being Looze Cannon. And I think that’s what the game is missing is just originality.”

“I always tell people, ‘Put a Prince filter on and see if you can dance with me in the same type of ring,’” he adds. “And if you can’t do that, then what you’re saying is just, in my eyes, just hate.”

When I suggest that the filters are still new, Cannon corrects me. “It’s not really new,” he says. “Anybody can put a filter on, but how can you bring it to life? People get so lost on, ‘Oh, I can put a filter on,’ and things like that. But after you put the filter on, you only have the attention span of a person for at least five to 10, 15 seconds max to lock them in, or they swiping somewhere else.”

“It takes a certain type of charisma to bring the filter to life because people want to really get into what’s happening,” he continues. “But if you’re just banking on a filter and talking like your regular self or not performing in a certain way, then it means nothing.”

Cannon is independent and says he’d been selling downloads directly to fans before “Big Michael Michael” took off.

“I’ve been pretty much direct-to-consumer because I’m an independent artist and I always was in the streaming world,” he says.

The appeal was how much a small group of fans could bring in. “I had to get the mindset of, you know what? Hey, if I have 50 loyal fans that’ll buy my download for $1.99, I’m beating a majority of the people that’s getting 100,000 streams,” he says. “But in the midst of that, I understand the times that we’re in and you got to play ball sometimes. And how this record took off, I knew that I had to service the platforms. So I did it, but I’ve always been direct-to-consumer for a long time now.”

He says the new listeners are finding his older music, too. “I’m actually seeing the numbers of my other songs and they are picking up. They skyrocketing right as well,” he says. “So people hear ‘Big Michael Michael’ and they’re like, ‘Oh wait, he has more music. Let me go check it out.’”

“My Spotify is up, my Apple Music is up,” Cannon adds. “I’m seeing people actually post my other records and doing videos to my other songs, so that’s a good sign.”

He says Snoop Dogg, Timbaland, and Usher have reached out, along with comedians Tiffany Haddish and Funny Marco. “I got a lot of celebrity friends now,” he says. “Uncle Snoop Dogg, that’s my guy.” Trending Stories Noel Fielding Says He Regrets 'Horrible' Jokes He Made With Russell Brand After Old Clip Resurfaces Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters Files for Divorce From Fourth Wife Kamilah Chavis After 5 Years of Marriage Journey Go Their Separate Ways With Longtime Drummer The ‘You Can See Everything’ Interview You’ve Been Waiting For

“I’ve been in the studio working with a few different talented artists from the Eric Bellingers, the Roscoe Dash, and many more,” he adds. “I’ll just say more for right now.”

Now, Looze Cannon is planning a project to follow the single. “Yes, I’m definitely about to drop a project because it’s time,” he says. “It’s time to show everybody that outside of my content that I do on social media, I’m a serious artist and I’m going to show the world that now that I got the eyes, it’s time to show them the prize.”

#3286. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

While phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

When you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives users a false sense of security.

Of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

There are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

On the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

When you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

On the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

Also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

College Football Playoff hopes are on the line tonight when the No. 6 Texas Longhorns face the No. 21 LSU Tigers at Death Valley in Baton Rouge.

The Longhorns are at 7-2 with three consecutive wins, including a decisive 34-20 victory over the No. 22 Missouri Tigers last weekend. LSU is at a solid 6-3, but they’re coming off a tough 31-13 home loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide.

It’s a critical game for both SEC teams, and the first time they’ll play as conference mates. They last met in 2019, when then-LSU quarterback Joe Burrow helped lead the Tigers to a 45-38 win.

If you don’t have a way to watch the Texas vs. LSU game tonight, read on. Ahead are a few ways to stream the game online without cable, including ways to get a free Texas vs. LSU livestream.

Texas and LSU face off on Saturday, Nov. 14. Kickoff is at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT. The game will be broadcast nationally on ABC.

Cord-cutters can watch the Texas vs. LSU football game online using any live TV streaming service that carries ABC or the ESPN Unlimited app. Below are your best options, including a few that offer free trials — use those to stream Texas vs. LSU for free without cable.

ABC is included in most DirecTV packages, including its smaller MyNews and MySports Genre Packs and all of its larger Streaming TV Packages. All DirecTV plans begin with a five-day free trial that you can use to watch Texas vs. LSU for free, and plans renew automatically starting at $39.99 after the trial ends.

Fubo is another great all-around live TV streamer that carries ABC in its Core and Ultra packages. Subscriptions start with a five-day free trial before plans renew starting at a discounted rate of $63.99.

YouTube TV carries ABC in both of its live TV streaming plans, and you get a free trial between five and 21 days to start. Once the trial ends, subscriptions renew at a discounted rate of $49.99 a month for the more affordable of the two plans.

Fans can also stream the Texas vs. LSU game online with ESPN Unlimited, which delivers all ESPN and ESPN on ABC content in one place. This is the most affordable option, with plans starting at $31.99 a month, but you don’t get a free trial as you do with the options above.

#3279. ‘Scream’ Actor C.W. Morgan’s Cause Of Death Revealed

A cause of death for Scream actor C.W. Morgan has been determined by the Los Angeles County Department of Medical Examiner: atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

Morgan, who died at 72 on August 30, played Hank Loomis, father of the one of the franchise’s Ghostface killers (played by Skeet Ulrich) and ex-husband of another (Scream 2‘s Laurie Metcalf) in 1996’s Scream and 2000’s Scream 3.

According to People magazine, Morgan’s official cause of death was atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, or a weakening and hardening of the arteries.

When Morgan’s death was first reported last month, the Los Angeles Police Department said the death was the result of natural causes. Watch on Deadline

Born Curtis Wade Morgan was in Bisbee, Arizona, Morgan launched his screen career on the NBC drama Midnight Caller in 1991. Other credits include the 1992 TV movie The Last of His Tribe, 1995’s Aeon Flux, the 1997 film Metro and a 2000 episode of Nash Bridges.

When I saw the price of the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder, my eyes bulged out of my head like a cartoon rabbit being chased by a mountain lion. $229? For an espresso machine… and a grinder? What year is this, 2001?

It’s hard to explain just how cheap $229 is, but I’ll do my best. The entry-level Casabrews Tornado grinder is $139 — and that’s seriously budget. The De’Longhi Stilosa espresso machine is $149 — and, again, that’s seriously budget. So $229 for a grinder and an espresso machine is literally unheard of.

So, how does the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder hold up? Well, it’s $229. That’s all I really have to say. While, yes, this is the cheapest bean-to-cup I’ve ever seen, it performs like it. But this might be enough to make it one of your best espresso machines if you’re on a budget best described as “as close to zero as possible”. Find out the full story in this Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder review.

2 x pressurized portafilters, scoop, tamper, tamping collar, brush

The Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is $229 from Amazon U.S. and £239 from Amazon U.K. On Amzchef’s website, the Espresso Machine with Grinder is listed as “All-in-One” espresso machine and is $299 rather than $229. The “Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder” is a completely different product with a different screen style — albeit $229, not $299. I've raised this with Amzchef and have been informed it will correct this inconsistency.

They don’t make it easy for us, huh? Anyway, I would buy from Amazon due to the lower price. For ease of searching, the product code is CM1626 — but Amzchef doesn’t list this on its website (for any of its products… just a wonderful, transparent business strategy, I know). The links above are to the Amazon page, not Amzchef’s site.

Opaque pricing aside, the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is incredibly cheap. As I wrote in my “Pros” section above, it’s almost unbelievably cheap. A bean-to-cup espresso machine for $229? Seriously? Most electric grinders start at $150, like the Casabrews Tornado or Breville Dose Control Pro.

The only machines I’ve tested around the same price are the $350 Gevi Espresso Machine with Grinder and the $350 Casabrews Marenza. While this machine is a seriously budget option, the low, low pricing does raise questions about longevity — which I’ll get into later.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

The Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder is a cheap coffee machine, and it feels like it. The scoop is flimsy plastic, and the dosing collar isn’t wide enough to allow the tamper to pass through. The tamper itself is lovely and weighty, though.

There’s no milk jug, which isn’t unprecedented, but is still a kick in the teeth. Casabrews also ships its budget machines with no milk jug, but it sells one for $10. Amzchef doesn’t sell a milk jug at all, so you’ll have to buy a separate one from another brand.

On top of that, the steam wand is supposed to have a 360° swivel, but I’d describe it more as 200° grating. Every time I moved the steam wand, the metal grated against the ball joint.

There’s a bright screen with full-color pictures, which also houses the built-in timer and temperature adjustment screen. This screen is the best part of the machine’s design, although I’m not sure it’s enough of a unique selling point to recommend buying it.

Considering the Amzchef Espresso Machine has a built-in grinder, I was extremely concerned when I unboxed two pressurized portafilter baskets. If you don’t know the difference between pressurized and non-pressurized baskets, I’ll give you a quick rundown. Pressurized portafilter baskets use two walls to force the espresso through a little hole, which creates fluffier crema but destroys delicate flavors. You should use pressurized portafilter baskets if you have pre-ground coffee or an inferior grinder (subtle foreshadowing).

Non-pressurized portafilter baskets have a mesh-like bottom, which allows the espresso to extract naturally, with no extra pressure — that all comes from the fineness of the grind. These baskets are a little trickier to use for beginners, but brew delicate, nuanced espresso if you have a good grinder and good beans.

So I was immediately suspicious when I saw the pressurized baskets. If I’m using a machine with a built-in grinder — ergo, freshly ground coffee — surely I should be provided non-pressurized baskets? A dual-walled basket will over-pressurize my espresso and mask delicate flavors.

Anyway, I had to use what Amzchef provided, so I, of course, tested it with said pressurized baskets.

By default, the grinder grinds for 7 seconds. This resulted in 17.3g of coffee during my tests, but obviously this will change if you grind finer or coarser for different beans. I set the grinder to click 5, as this pulled the ideal 1:2 ratio in 25-28 seconds.

Then, the machine automatically doses water. It pulled 35g of coffee in 28 seconds, which is almost the perfect 1:2 ratio in 25-28 seconds.

Here’s a photo of said default shot. This is with zero customizations — straight from the machine’s brain.

The crema is a little flat, and there’s not a whole lot of depth to the shot. I usually love watching the black ‘body’ of the shot rise up after extraction, but that wasn’t the case with this espresso. It brewed this dark amber color and this dark amber color it remained. As for the taste, it was a little bitter, not particularly strong or weak, but it got the job done. If you’re a total beginner, this would be good enough, but coffee enthusiasts would be better off elsewhere.

However, coffee enthusiasts might be the intended target audience here. There are a few premium, coffee snob-certified features on the Amzchef. You’ve got a PID controller, which controls water temperature, and you can customize temps to your liking. It can go from 190°-201°F, more versatile than Breville’s set-at-200°F PID controller, which you’d find on the $299 Breville Bambino or the $499 Breville Bambino Plus.

All of these features are excellent — I wouldn’t buy an espresso machine without — and resulted in decent espresso. Pressurized portafilters aside, this coffee sits firmly in the “good enough” category. Especially for $229, which is crazy cheap.

I have never seen a bean-to-cup semi-automatic espresso machine cheaper than the Amzchef Espresso Machine with Grinder. I’ve tested $350 models — the aforementioned Casabrews Marenza and Gevi Espresso Machine with Grinder — but $229? That’s crazy cheap.

The grinder itself has 44 settings, so you can grind from superfine to cold-brew-coarse. As mentioned earlier, the grinder grinds for 7 seconds by default, which you can adjust. To test uniformity, I used my Kruve Coffee Sieves ($189). As espresso grounds should be 300-400 microns, I sift ground coffee through the 500-micron sieve. I’m looking for 100% pass-through. I used click 5 to test espresso, which extracted a 1:2 ratio in 28 seconds.

Here’s a photo to exemplify what I mean. The left is coffee bigger than 500 microns, and the right is coffee smaller than 500 microns (espresso size).

As you can see, this is a non-uniform, inconsistent grinder… and now I know why Amzchef only provides you dual-walled portafilters.

The steam wand is one of the biggest let-dows of the whole machine. It’s weak, spluttery, and takes over sixty seconds to steam a jug of milk (for one coffee).

To activate the steam wand itself, you have to press the steam graphic on the screen, not twist the knob on the side. After pressing the graphic, and the machine reading 107 (temperature), then you twist the knob. It needs a few seconds to switch to steam.

However, the steam wand is really disappointing. I still managed to get half-decent latte art, but the actual texture of the milk was undesirable. It had a layer of foam on top and then wet milk — no velvety aeration throughout.

As you can see, the latte art is still good. But this is after years of practice. I don’t think this is a good machine for beginners to learn on, because you have to know how to tease out “good” milk texture from a sub-par wand.

I don’t really have anything positive to say about the steam wand. If you aren’t fussed about milk drinks, this might be something you can overlook, but for me, I live for decadent, velvety milk, so it’d be a pass.

As it’s just 13 inches wide and 13 inches deep, the Amzchef Espresso Machine is relatively compact, especially for a bean-to-cup machine. If you’re seriously short on space (and budget), I might recommend the Amzchef, but that’s a might.

The machine has an “aluminum alloy” boiler, which means it’s more susceptible to corrosion than a stainless steel boiler, however, there’s no water filter slot in the water tank. Either the machine won’t last as long as a stainless steel boiler, or you’ll need to be seriously on top of descaling — even if you live in a soft water area. There are also no cleaning discs or a cleaning portafilter basket cover for backflushing, unlike Breville and De’Longhi’s machines.

Amzchef advertizes a 2-year warranty if you purchase from the Amzchef website, but the espresso machine is $70 more expensive on the Amzchef site (at time of writing — Amzchef has told me it will correct this). If you register it, the warranty increases to three years. However, you have to spend an extra $70 buying it directly from Amzchef. On the Amzchef warranty page, it reads, “Buy from Amazon, Walmart, or other online retailers? You may get an up-to-2-year limited warranty.” Schrödinger’s warranty!

Amzchef’s representative confirmed that you receive a 2-year warranty regardless of retailer, which is great news, but the language is still too opaque. What if you didn’t have a direct link to the company to find out this information (as I assume most of you won’t)? The language needs to be clearer.

Opaque business practices like this make me incredibly wary about recommending a product. It’s disingenuous. I wouldn’t spend my hard-earned money at a company with obfuscated warranty rules.

Everything about the Amzchef Espresso Machine feels too good to be true. A PID controller, customizable brew temperature, built-in grinder, cold brew, and 360° swivel steam wand for $229? There’s something not quite right here — and you can feel it in the build quality. The water tank is flimsy, the grinder hopper is flimsy, the portafilter is flimsy, and the steam wand grates as it moves. Not only that, but the steam wand is relatively weak, and the low-quality grinder makes for mediocre espresso.

This is a tricky one, because $229 is incredibly cheap for an espresso machine with a grinder. Normally, you’d be expecting to pay $229 for the espresso machine alone and an extra $229 for the grinder — and that would be cheap.

However, I can’t recommend this machine due to its low-quality build, low-quality accessories, and low-quality grinder. I would recommend grabbing the $350 Casabrews Marenza instead (but that’s also incredibly flimsy), or save up more for the Breville Barista Express — often around $499 during sales events like Black Friday — or the De’Longhi Arte Evo — also around $450 during sales events.

#3277. Skip Hinnant Dies: ‘Electric Company’, ‘You’re A Good Man, Charlie Brown’ Actor, Voice Of Fritz The Cat Was 86

Skip Hinnant, an original cast member of PBS’ The Electric Company in the 1970s and the prolific voice actor behind Fritz the Cat, My Little Pony and 1977’s stop-motion Easter Bunny, died Sunday, November 8, in Denver. He was 86.

His death was announced by his family, who noted he passed peacefully surrounded by loved ones.

Born Joseph Howard Hinnant on September 12, 1940, and raised on Chincoteague Island, Virginia, Hinnant got his start in television as a recurring character from 1963 to 1965 on ABC’s identical cousins sitcom The Patty Duke Show; he played the boyfriend of Duke’s Cathy (Eddie Applegate played the boyfriend of Duke’s Patty).

After originating the role of Schroeder in the Off Broadway musical You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown (1967) – other cast members included Gary Burghoff as Charlie Brown, Bob Balaban as Linus and Hinnant’s late brother Bill Hinnant as Snoopy – Hinnant began expanding to voice work, including a 1969 episode of Sesame Street and, perhaps most famously, as the voice behind Fritz the Cat, the star character in Ralph Bakshi’s adult-oriented animation films based on the work of underground artist Robert Crumb. Hinnant voiced the role in the original X-rated Fritz the Cat (1972) and its 1974 R-rated sequel The Nine Lives of Fritz the Cat. Watch on Deadline

In 1971, Hinnant became an original featured performer in PBS’ kids show The Electric Company, where over the next six years and 780 episodes he would play the roles of Fargo North, Frankenstein, Jay-Jay and Supper Man, among others. His castmates included Morgan Freeman, Rita Moreno and Bill Cosby.

Hinnant voiced the title character in the 1977 Rankin/Bass stop-motion Easter special The Easter Bunny is Comin’ to Town.

Other voice credits include the 1970s cartoon series Spidey Super Stories, the 1980 stop-motion film I Go Pogo (he was Pogo Possum), various roles on My Little Pony from 1986-1987, the 1990 TV movie Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day and, that same year, HBO Storybook Musicals.

In the late 1980s he had onscreen roles in single episodes of As the World Turns (1988) and Kate & Allie (1989).

Hinnant was an active union member of Actor’s Equity, AFTRA, and Screen Actors Guild, serving on the national board of SAG from 1980 to 2003. His family notes that he “was proud of his work to preserve commercial voice contracts and the everyday actor’s rights.”

Hinnant is survived by longtime partner Ruth Nerken; children Chris, Jamie, Julie and Sara, and their spouses; nine grandchildren; and his ex-wife Miriam Hinnant.

#3275. Google DeepMind analysis proves Signal and WhatsApp encryption is secure

The Signal protocol has long been considered the gold standard for end-to-end encrypted messaging, with Edward Snowden a notable advocate. Now a Google DeepMind analysis has “formally verified” the security of the protocol.

In addition to its use in the Signal app, the same protocol is also used by WhatsApp and Google Messages, and the work has been described as “a landmark development” …

“Formal verification” is the term given to mathematically proving or disproving that a cryptographic algorithm or protocol satisfies its security claims under all conditions. It guarantees that there is no situation in which the protocol will fail. This is a far higher standard than traditional testing methods which seek to find vulnerabilities but cannot promise that others do not exist.

Using agentic AI to carry out formal verification is a huge breakthrough for cryptography and AI alike. It is, however, extremely computationally demanding, so Google told Wired it’s unclear as yet how practical it will be to use it more broadly.

DeepMind researchers emphasize that their findings are just one milestone in a larger process. “We are very excited by this result, but there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world, and we want to do that,” Swarat Chaudhuri, a DeepMind research scientist, tells WIRED.

It’s important to note that the validation is for the protocol itself rather than the Signal app as a whole. However, encouragement can be taken from the fact that when tested against older versions of Signal that contained known vulnerabilities, it identified those and flagged them as failing formal verification.

Also worth stating is that Google was able to build on some past formal verification work already completed without the use of AI. This analysis took four weeks, and the scale of resources required has not yet been disclosed, so we shouldn’t expect a whole array of other protocols to be validated overnight. All the same, this is a very big deal.

#3274. Penélope Cruz Guarded Against Marital Blowback Playing Opposite Javier Bardem In ‘Bunker’: “You Are Touching Things That Are Delicate” – Contenders L.A.

Penélope Cruz revealed that she had concerns that the fragile relationship between the husband-and-wife leads of filmmaker Florian Zeller’s Bunker might bleed over into her rock-solid union with husband Javier Bardem.

“We’ve worked together every five or six years – we don’t plan it like that, but I think in a way we both want to protect and we feel like if we would be working together too often, it would be tricky and risky,” Cruz explained during a panel at Deadline’s Contenders Film Los Angeles event Saturday at the DGA Theater. “But when Florian came to us, even before we read the script, we looked at each other and we knew none of us would want to say no … because we were huge fans and now even more after working with him.

RELATED: ‘Bunker’ Venice Film Festival Red Carpet Photos: Paul Dano, Penélope Cruz, Javier Bardem, Stephen Graham & More

“There was no way we were going to say no. And we came into this adventure with him. And even if it was challenging at times, for example, for the big fight scene, we did that during three days and it was terrifying to me because we had to go into places that were really, really uncomfortable,” Cruz added, referencing the couple’s crucial confrontation in the film.

“Even if it’s not your real story, it doesn’t matter,” she said. “You know you are touching things that are delicate. And we always felt his protection and his guidance. And it was more the fear of the week before doing it than, actually, the process of doing that scene that I was obsessed with.”

RELATED: Javier Bardem & Penélope Cruz Talk Playing Fictitious Arguing Couple In ‘Bunker’: “We Are Very Good At Creating Fiction & Reality” – Venice

She told Zeller, who joined her on the panel: “And then you made us enjoy doing that scene. You made us enjoy every single step of the process, but you know how terrified I was of that scene the week before I became a total nightmare. I know.”

RELATED: ‘Bunker’ Review: Penélope Cruz And Javier Bardem’s Marriage Is In Crisis In Florian Zeller’s Drama Of Isolation And Fears – Venice Film Festival

“They are extraordinary actors as we know,” said Zeller. “And it’s always such a joy for a filmmaker to have the opportunity to look at beautiful human beings and actors, but I have to say that I was also very interested to have them together onscreen, because as we know, you are in a couple in real life, and I thought it would be an extraordinary opportunity to explore something unique, something that has to do with the truth, with authenticity.

“Not to say that this is their story — because it is not, obviously — but because they are great actors, they are digging into themselves to find the truth, to find authenticity.”

“I’m sure you remember Eyes Wide Shut. At the time, Nicole Kimman and Tom Cruise, they were a real couple when they did this beautiful film with Kubrick,” Zeller explained. “And I remember that I mentioned this to [Cruz] and to Javier also when we first talked about the film, because I remember as a viewer, the excitement to be in a position when you do not know exactly what you’re invited to watch. Again, is it fiction? Is it the truth? Is it another version of the truth?”

RELATED: ‘Bunker’ Clip: Watch Javier Bardem & Penélope Cruz In Florian Zeller’s Venice-Bound Psychological Thriller

He added: “But I also remember Javier saying, ‘You should not mention this film too often because at the end of the shooting, they broke up.’ And then I also realized that Kubrick soon died just after the shooting. So I was like, ‘OK, I’m not going to mention this.’

“But the real difference is in Bunker, the destination of what we tried to do is really the reconciliation, how to feel the reconnection between two people who love them themselves and have been disconnected,” the filmmaker said.

#3271. John Turturro, Tatiana Maslany Created Raw Estrangement In ‘The Only Living Pickpocket In New York’ – Contenders L.A.

John Turturro and Tatiana Maslany have one scene together in The Only Living Pickpocket in New York. When Harry (Turturro) shows up on her doorstep, it has been years since they’ve seen each other. Both actors prepared for the scene, but Turturro had an idea to keep it raw. At Deadline’s Contenders Film Los Angeles, he shared what he told writer/director Noah Segan on the day of the scene.

“I just suggested to Noah, let’s just block it, let’s not rehearse it,” Turturro said. “They haven’t seen each other in such a long time. So we never rehearsed it. The rawness is evident. We did the master, then Tatiana and myself.”

Harry is the pickpocket of the title. It becomes apparent through their conversation that Harry was not around and resented her for moving out of the city. Watch on Deadline

RELATED: ‘The Only Living Pickpocket In New York’ Review: John Turturro Steals The Show In Noah Segan’s Mesmerizing Debut – Sundance Film Festival

“The writing is so elegant,” Maslany said. “There’s a lot of space between moments where things are unsaid. I just thought it was a really gorgeous scene. The idea of doing a scene with so much history in it, when you have only four pages or whatever to do it.”

Maslany did her own preparation, but said she remained present to respond to what Turturro had prepared.

“I bring everything that I’ve worked on, obviously, to that day but then it’s about being present with that person opposite you,” she said. “John is so full up on this character. He’s so deep it was very easy to feel that history even though we only had a morning to do it.”

RELATED: Watch Your Wallet: John Turturro Turns Master Thief For Noah Segan’s Wistful Crime Thriller ‘The Only Living Pickpocket In New York’ — Sundance Q&A

Harry lifts a flash drive from tech guy (Will Price) connected to the mob. He spends the day trying to get it back. With mobsters in pursuit, there is violent crime in the film.

“The violence in the movie is usually offscreen but the cost of the violence, the effect of it is on screen,” Turturro said. “That’s what we carry with us.”

For one confrontation at gunpoint, Turturro recalled a terrifying incident from his past. In the ‘70s, at 2 a.m. one night, he pulled up to a basketball court where a man was shooting hoops. That man was a police officer who pulled a gun on Turturro, concerned he was suspicious at that hour. Turturro cleared it up and they ended up playing.

“I could barely move my legs, I was so full of lactic acid,” he said. “I remember the gun to my head. There’s no more dignity left for this particular guy so you have to give the performance of your life but it’s real.”

For Harry’s day job, Turturro studied pickpocketing methods with magician and pickpocket Apollo Robbins. Harry works alone, which is unusual.

“Usually they work in teams,” Turturro said. “A man and a woman would work together. Usually, it was the woman who would pickpocket. They had their own morality. They didn’t rob people who were inebriated or handicapped or really old. They found a mark who was wealthy. The idea is you don’t pull something out. You set them up in a way they don’t feel it. You move the person. The person doesn’t feel it’s gone.”
